messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: prometheus scrape failures detected for job=redwood-scrapers (metrics: inference_serving_requests_total, inference_serving_latency, log_ingest_consumer_lag). 90% of targets in eu-west-1 failing (connection reset / 503). PagerDuty incident PDR-83421 created and page sent to #eng-sre oncall. root_ts=1763005123

alex: acked oncall (PDR-83421). I'm looking. first glance: prometheus targets show repeated TLS handshake errors and 502/connection reset. grafana alert shows spike in embedding request 5xxs.

maria: adding context — we rolled retention/forwarding change on log-ingest-consumer yesterday evening (PR #482). That increased throughput to kafka and we saw some consumer lag but assumed autoscale handled it. tagging ops.

sam: I can grab prometheus logs / exporter status. which cluster is this?

alex: eu-west-1 prometheus server (prom-p-3). kubectl context: prod-eu.

alex: running quick checks:
```
kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=prometheus-prom-p-3
kubectl -n monitoring logs prometheus-prom-p-3 -c prometheus | tail -n 200
curl -v https://10.2.5.12:9090/targets | jq '.data.activeTargets[] | select(.health=="down")' | head
```

sam: logs show repeated "upstream connect error: connection reset by peer" to exporter endpoints 10.4.x.x (inference-serving-exporter) and 10.6.x.x (log-ingest-exporter). Also TLS handshake errors: "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" on some endpoints.

maria: hmm cert errors — did we rotate certs for internal mTLS? I deployed cert-bot patch yesterday for node cert renewal but it was limited to staging. Not sure it touched prod.

alex: I'm seeing high TCP connections on the exporter side, cpu flapping on exporter pods, OOM restarts? replica set for inference-serving-exporter is at 70% CPU but heap stable. exporter logs show "accept: too many open files" intermittently. kernel fd limit hit?

ops-bot: Auto-scaling event: deployment/log-ingest-exporter scaled from 3 -> 1 due to HPA glitch at 2026-03-05T10:01Z (recent change: metricName changed in HPA config). See k8s-alert: hpa-misconfigured.

alex: oh that explains partial capacity. I'm going to bump replicas for exporters and restart prometheus scrape targets that are flapping. Doing quick manual remediation:
```
kubectl -n inference set resources deploy/inference-serving-exporter --limits=cpu=1000m --requests=500m
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/inference-serving-exporter --replicas=4
kubectl -n logs scale deploy/log-ingest-exporter --replicas=3
kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart statefulset/prom-p-3
```

maria: I'll open a PD escalation to L4 in parallel. Paging l4-oncall now. @l4-oncall can you join? PDR-83421, reason: mass scrape failures impacting metrics and customer-facing 5xxs.

l4-oncall: joining. pulled logs. Confirmed HPA misconfig + file descriptor exhaustion on exporters. Looks like HPA target metric name change from PR #521 silently left prod HPA without metrics -> scaled down to min (1).

sam: reconfig'd HPA to use cpu and queue_depth fallback. Pushed quickfix PR to prod HPA: revert metricName change. PR #526.

alex: after scaling exporters up and restarting prom, targets are slowly turning green. current: 60% up -> 95% up in last 3m. embedding 5xx rate dropped from 11.8% to 3.2% (grafana panel). Latency back to baseline for most routes.

maria: customer impact note: internal SLO alert triggered; we saw increased error-rate on hosted API for embeddings and chat generation between 09:58–10:14 UTC. Estimated impacted requests ~12k, error budget burn ~0.7%. Notified support to flag high-severity customers if they reach out.

alex: let's keep prometheus in debug for another 20m, and monitor fd counts on exporters. Also will bump node limits for file descriptors on exporter nodes (sysctl fs.file-max / container ulimit) as an intermediate fix.

ops-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prometheus-scrape-failures — checklist updated with HPA rollback step and exporter fd tuning.

sam: added a one-off cron to rotate exporter logs less frequently to avoid causing excessive FD use. Also adding livenessProbe tweak to tolerate short spikes while autoscale recovers.

l4-oncall: recommend follow-ups: 1) revert HPA metric change in config repo, 2) add CI guard for HPA metricName mismatches, 3) increase exporter replica default to 3, 4) audit cert rotations for internal mTLS. Creating follow-up task: INT-1159.

maria: will own INT-1159 (postmortem + action items). tagging support and product for customer comms draft.

alex: will keep monitoring until we have 30 minutes of stable metrics. For now incident status: mitigated. PDR-83421: acknowledged -> resolved once stable.

sam: small note for oncall handoff: current state stable, but watch HPA metrics and file descriptors; set a temporary alert for exporter_fd_usage > 80% with 2m window.

maria: thanks team. I'll write the incident summary and postmortem. closing thread when PDR is resolved and INT-1159 created. :white_check_mark:

pagerbot: PAGERDUTY: PDR-83421 marked mitigated at 1763005600. Escalation log attached.

alex: resolved and marking this thread resolved. final numbers: impacted requests ~12k, peak 5xx rate 12.1%, mitigation reduced to baseline in ~16m.

maria: postmortem draft: "Prometheus scrape outages caused by HPA misconfiguration and exporter file-descriptor exhaustion after log-ingest throughput increase. Immediate mitigations: scale exporters, restart prom, revert HPA metricName. Longer-term: CI guard, fd tuning, default replica bump, cert rotation audit."

sam: ack. leaving note: we should add exporter metrics (fd_usage, open_files) to alert rules.

ops-bot: Incident PDR-83421 closed. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prometheus-scrape-failures.

maria: marking last_message_ts now. closing thread. Thanks all!
